title: Spiced Mango Chutney
summary: Chunks of ripe mango simmered with mustard seeds, ginger, warm spices, brown sugar and cider vinegar into a glossy, sweet and tangy chutney.

ingredients.item: ripe but firm mango flesh, cut in 1.5 cm dice
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Bloom the seeds
steps.text: Heat the oil in the saucepan over a medium heat, add the mustard seeds and chilli flakes and cook until the seeds start to pop, 30-60 seconds. Frying whole spices first releases their flavour into the oil.

steps.title: Soften the onion
steps.text: Add the onion and cook for about 5 minutes, stirring, until soft and lightly golden. Stir in the ginger, garlic, cinnamon, cloves and garam masala and cook 1 minute more.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add the mango, sugar, vinegar, water and salt and bring to the boil. Lower the heat and simmer, stirring often and more frequently towards the end, for 30-40 minutes until thick and glossy and a spoon dragged across the base leaves a clear trail.

steps.title: Jar
steps.text: Spoon the hot chutney into clean, hot jars, seal and cool. It thickens further as it cools.

tips: Choose mangoes that are ripe but still firm so the pieces hold their shape.
A common mistake is stopping too early; it should look thick and jammy in the pan, as it only firms slightly as it cools.
Stir more often near the end, as the sugar catches easily on the base of the pan.
Let it mature for a few days in the fridge; the flavours mellow and blend.
storage: Keep in sealed jars in the fridge for up to 2 months. Use a clean spoon each time. It can be frozen for up to 6 months. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
